subject: TekPath / Redwood: solution validation kickoff and test plan
messages:
From: Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@tekpath.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: TekPath / Redwood: solution validation kickoff

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week — TekPath is excited to move forward on the joint integration validation. We put together a short reference design and a smoke-test plan that we'd like to run with Redwood's SE team to validate routing, auth, and the recommended cache/batch settings for our integration.

High-level asks:
- Can Redwood run the validation against a TekPath dev sandbox (we'll provide creds) next week?
- Primary goals: correct model routing for fallbacks, stable latency under a 3–5 QPS baseline, and end-to-end tracing across the call path.

I've copied Mike (ops) on logistics. Attached are the reference design and an initial test plan; please confirm who from Redwood should own the run and any preferred time windows.

Attachments: [tekpath-reference-design.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)], [tekpath-validation-test-plan.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)]

Thanks,
Sara Mueller
Sr. Solutions Architect | TekPath Solutions
+sara.mueller@tekpath.com | +1 415-555-0123

--

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@tekpath.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TekPath / Redwood: solution validation kickoff

Sara — great, thanks for sending the docs. Marcus and Laura are looped in to schedule and lead the validation.

Quick responses:
- We can run the smoke tests against a TekPath dev sandbox — please send service account creds (preferred: ephemeral key + CIDR allowlist) and an endpoint URL.
- Laura will own the runtime config and will run an initial baseline test to collect latency and KV cache profiles.
- Can you also confirm expected model(s) and approximate QPS distribution (burst vs sustained)? That helps us pick the right model variant and batching profile.

I've also added a link to our partner-runbook that has the standard checklist for environment prep: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bTekPathShared/runbook (internal). If you can upload the TekPath environment variables and any test tokens there, that will speed things up.

Propose we schedule a 30-min validation kickoff tomorrow 09:00–09:30 PT or Thursday 14:00–14:30 PT — Marcus, Laura, Priyom, and I can make either.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@tekpath.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Hamilton <mike.hamilton@tekpath.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TekPath / Redwood: solution validation kickoff

Thanks Jonas — attaching the files you requested and answering your Qs inline: 

- Model(s): TekPath will use an open LLM (gpt-open-3) for routing in prod, but our dev sandbox exposes gpt-open-3-alpha (reduced params). Please validate routing policy against both variants if possible.
- Expected QPS: baseline 3 QPS sustained, bursts up to 15 QPS for short periods (peak < 2 minutes).
- Auth: We'll provide an ephemeral service account JSON and a CIDR allowlist for your IPs.

Attachments included: [tekpath-reference-design.pdf], [tekpath-validation-test-plan.xlsx]

I've also created a shared folder with sample traces and a Postman collection: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bTekPathShared

We'll be available for the 09:00 PT slot tomorrow. Looking forward to it.

Cheers,
Sara

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@tekpath.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TekPath / Redwood: solution validation kickoff

Hi Sara — Laura from Redwood SE here. Thanks for the materials, very helpful. A few clarifying questions before the kickoff (copied so we have a short agenda):

1) Auth & routing
- Ephemeral service account JSON is perfect. Can you confirm the auth header format (Bearer token vs. HMAC) and expected TTL for the token?

2) Model mapping / fallback
- You mentioned routing to gpt-open-3 and a dev alpha. Do you expect Redwood to do automatic fallback between variants, or will TekPath return a routing decision in the request payload?

3) Caching & KV size
- The reference design notes a per-user KV cache of ~12MB. Is that the working assumption for our capacity calculations, or is that a peak number? Also, do you anticipate cold-starts to be common when users hit a new session?

4) Batching and latency targets
- Baseline latency SLO we should validate against is 300ms p50 / 700ms p95 for simple prompts. Is that acceptable? We will run two modes: continuous batching (to optimize cost) and single-request low-latency mode so we can compare tradeoffs.

5) Test harness and artifacts
- Can you confirm the Postman collection points to the sandbox endpoints (so we can run the same script)? Also would appreciate any sample traces you can share in the shared folder.

Agenda suggestion for kickoff (30 mins): 1) confirm creds & network, 2) run a short baseline sample, 3) review trace and fallback behavior, 4) agree next steps.

If that looks good I'll send a calendar invite for 09:00 PT tomorrow and we can run the baseline in the first 10 minutes.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@tekpath.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jul 2025 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TekPath / Redwood: solution validation kickoff

Laura — perfect, thanks for the detailed questions. Confirming:
- Auth: Bearer token with 1h TTL, we'll issue an ephemeral service account and add Redwood's IPs to the allowlist before 08:00 PT tomorrow.
- Routing: TekPath can advertise a routing hint in the request payload (preferred); we also support request-level retry if Redwood wants automatic fallback.
- KV cache: 12MB is a target working size (typical session). Cold-starts are infrequent for active users.
- Latency SLO: 300ms p50 / 700ms p95 is acceptable as a validation target.
- Postman collection: yes, it points to the sandbox URLs and includes example payloads.

I'll upload the ephemeral service account and the Postman collection to the shared folder and send the calendar invite for 09:00 PT tomorrow. We'll also drop a short smoke-test CSV artifact after the run (TekPath-smoke-results.csv).

Looking forward to the run — speak tomorrow.

Best,
Sara Mueller
Sr. Solutions Architect | TekPath Solutions
